## **The role**
The Software Implementation Engineer is a hands-on technical delivery role at the centre of complex NHS deployments. At Heidi, the CSM owns the customer from day one: the relationship, the rollout plan, the path to renewal. The Implementation Engineer is the technical arm they lean on: the person who personally configures SSO with the customer's IT team, sets up and provisions tenants, delivers EHR integrations through to go-live, configures agents and custom builds, and gives every technical problem a fast diagnosis and the right owner — fixing what is configuration, and handing confirmed product defects to Support Engineering, who own and drive their resolution.
You are the reason launches don't stall on technical topics. The remit is deliberately broad: anything to do with getting an account set up, configured and optimised is yours, from account configuration and MFA through to integration build and iteration, rather than being split across several specialist roles.
Clinical training and adoption sit with Clinical Enablement, not here. Your ownership begins upon acceptance of the enterprise handover. It ends when the agreed technical scope has passed its acceptance criteria, customer sign-off has been recorded, the final configuration has been documented and the implementation has transferred into hypercare or BAU support.
You are technically credible in front of a CIO, precise in what you hand to engineers, and relentless about closing the loop — and you translate what customers need technically into clear, prioritised asks for the Technical Program Manager (TPM), who owns the integration roadmap and prioritisation.
**Success in this role looks like:**
* **Hands-on delivery —** you personally set up, configure and validate the technical footprint of an account: identity, provisioning, integrations, agents, data flows. Not coordinated — done.
* **Technical ownership —** every technical problem at your accounts gets a fast diagnosis and a clear owner. What is configuration or implementation, you fix; what is a product defect, Support Engineering owns and drives — you hand it over with the diagnosis attached and do not shadow the ticket. CSMs never have to diagnose or route technical problems themselves.
* **Fast unblocking —** technical blockers that would stall a launch for weeks get diagnosed, sequenced and resolved in days, because you understand the problem and know exactly who has to do what.
* **Clean boundaries —** you hand net-new build work to FDEs as precise, prioritised requirements they can act on without rework, and you route live product defects to Support Engineering with a proper diagnosis attached — you don’t hoard work that belongs elsewhere, and you don’t toss problems over walls.
* **Trusted translation —** customer IT and security teams treat you as a peer; the Technical Program Manager (TPM) gets integration gaps and technical priorities from you they can act on, and product hears a clear, prioritised signal.
This is a delivery-accountable role, so your job is to make the technical side of every account work: identity live, tenants configured, integrations delivered, agents built, security questions answered, and technical problems solved before they become escalations.
**What you’ll do**
**Technical Onboarding & Account Setup**
* Own the technical setup of new enterprise accounts end to end: tenant and workspace configuration, user provisioning and seat structure, environment readiness.
* Configure SSO with the customer’s IT team — SAML / OIDC against Okta, Microsoft Entra and NHS identity infrastructure — including MFA and conditional-access alignment.
* Drive network and device readiness: whitelisting, VDI and shared-device constraints, mobile device management, so clinicians can actually use Heidi on day one. Work directly with customer IT to clear whatever is blocking a swift deployment: deployment questionnaires, IT vetting, access requests, environment prerequisites.
**Integration Delivery**
* Receive the validated integration design and signed SOW from presales. Confirm implementation prerequisites, elaborate the agreed design where necessary, configure the Heidi components, perform technical testing, support customer UAT and execute the technical go-live activities within the implementation plan you own.
* Translate the agreed SOW and technical design into precise, prioritised implementation requirements; hand net-new build to FDEs in a form they can act on without rework, own the account-side delivery around it, and surface integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager. Raise any requirement that is missing, materially different or genuinely out of scope through formal change control before work proceeds, rather than absorbing scope creep silently.
* Provide credible estimates, identify dependencies early and give the CSM evidence-based status and recovery options. You own the integrated technical plan, customer-facing delivery dates and dependency escalation. After go-live, keep working with the trust integration team to iterate and optimise the integration: anything that is not a product defect is yours to make work.
**Product-technical Configuration**
* Set up agentic workflows, agents and custom builds to fit each account’s clinical and operational workflows, turning vague customer asks into scoped configurations with clear acceptance criteria.
* Translate what the customer bought into what has to be configured, and set it up: products, identity, integrations, agents, APIs, exports and data flows. As Heidi adds products (agents, agentic workflows, comms), their account-level setup lands here too.
* Handle technical template and coding setup where it crosses into system behaviour (clinical content stays with Clinical Enablement).
**Technical Escalation & Resolution**
* During active implementation and hypercare, be the first technical port of call for CSMs: when something technical breaks or will not configure, you provide first-line diagnosis and make sure it lands with the right owner. Once an account has formally handed over to BAU, Support Engineering owns initial triage and ongoing incident management, and you are re-engaged only through agreed escalation criteria.
* Diagnose before you route: implementation-phase and account-specific configuration issues are yours to fix; confirmed product defects go to Support Engineering with your diagnosis attached — they own and drive resolution, and Support Engineering owns defect resolution. The Implementation Engineer remains informed where the defect affects implementation milestones, acceptance criteria or customer readiness, without duplicating Support’s investigation.
* Translate customer technical problems into clear priorities — routing integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager (who owns the roadmap) and confirmed defects to Support Engineering — the alignment that gets problems actually solved.
**Information Governance & Security Enablement**
* Provide accurate technical input and evidence for DPIAs, security questionnaires and IT-assurance requests, routed through Compliance, who owns these processes. Security, Privacy and Clinical Safety retain approval authority for their respective positions. Keep them off the critical path without becoming the sign-off owner.
* Work within NHS governance gates — clinical safety sign-off, IG approval, change-control windows — planning technical work around them (clinical-safety substance is owned by Heidi’s Clinical Safety Officer).
**Handover acceptance and scope control**
* Review the signed SOW, discovery notes, technical decision record, architecture, acceptance criteria, success measures and open risk log before technical implementation begins.
* Return the handover where a blocking material risk, unclear scope or unsupported commitment prevents a credible implementation plan.
* Deliver against the agreed scope without converting new customer requirements into configuration work.
* Classify emerging requests as in-scope configuration, defect, net-new engineering, roadmap request or commercial change.
* Escalate material scope changes through the CSM, SE and AE before committing work or dates.
**How we show up**
* **Build for the next decade, not next quarter**. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.
* **Lead, don't wait**. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.
* **Follow the evidence**. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.
* **Own the outcome**. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.
* **Ship, measure, go again**. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.
* **Live in clinicians' reality**. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.
**Why Heidi?**
You’ll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who’ve felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.
Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn’t *whether* AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you’re doing the defining work of your career.
**Our Benefits**
* **Equity from day one.** When Heidi wins, you win. You'll share directly in the success you help create.
* **Your health, covered.** Comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, plus 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder and a £100/month Healthy Heidi’s stipend.
* **Global parental leave**. 26 weeks paid for primary carers and 18 weeks for secondary carers, subject to eligibility.
* **Fertility support**. £7,000 one-off payment, eligibility applies.
* **Learning & development.** £700 per year for courses, books, memberships, conferences and more.
* **Home office budget** of £500 one-off to set up a workspace you actually want to work in.
* **Recharge days** after major milestones and busy periods so you can reset and come back strong.
* **Work from anywhere** for up to 4 weeks per year, wherever the world takes you.
* **Clinical leave**. 10 days per year for eligible clinical roles to maintain accreditation and requirements.
* **Flexibility that works.** A hybrid environment, with 3 days in the office.

# Accuracy Checking Technician (ACT)
Royal Leamington Spa
Ready to revolutionize healthcare, making it faster and more accessible than ever before?
**How we started:**
Founded in 2013 by Dwayne D’Souza, HeliosXwas built on a simple but powerful idea: healthcare should be easier to access, faster to receive, and centred around the individual. From day one, we’ve grown without external funding; scaling profitably through technology, disciplined execution, and deep medical expertise. What started as a challenger idea has become one of the most significant healthcare platforms operating globally today.
**Where we are now:**
We’ve earned the trust of millions of people worldwide through category-leading products and well-known brands, including MedExpress, Dermatica, ZipHealth, RocketRX, and Levity. A key driver of our success is vertical integration; we operate our own manufacturing and proprietary products, led by in-house medical teams, researchers, and pharmacists at the top of their fields.
In 2025, HeliosX treated more than 1.7 million patients globally and reached £781m in revenue, representing +337% year-on-year growth and cementing our position as the clear market leader in the UK. That growth translates into real-world outcomes: our weight-loss treatments helped patients lose 8.5 million kilograms of excess weight in 2025 alone, contributing to an estimated 1,300 fewer cardiac events. This is growth with measurable, life-changing impact at scale.
Today, we operate across four international markets, with successful launches in Germany and Canada and continued expansion in the US. We were also recently recognised in the Sunday Times Top 100 fastest-growing tech companies, further validation of both our momentum and our ambition.
**Where we’re going:**
2026 is another significant year for HeliosX. Our ambition is to surpass £1.1bn in revenue, continue expanding thoughtfully into new international markets and broaden our condition and treatment portfolio. As we scale, we're focused on building the technology, operational excellence and clinical capabilities that will support sustainable long-term growth. Joining HeliosX now means helping shape the systems, teams and products that will define the next chapter of digital healthcare. You'll be solving complex problems at pace, working alongside exceptional people and building products that genuinely improve lives at scale.
**There’s never been a more exciting time to join HeliosX. Come be a part of making our dream of easier and faster healthcare a reality!**
### **About the Role:**
We’re looking for a qualified Accuracy Checking Technician to join our Pharmacy team and play a key role in ensuring every prescription is checked accurately and safely before reaching our patients. This role will be responsible for the final accuracy check of dispensed prescription items, making sure the right medicine, right strength, right patient and right label are delivered every time

* Maintain accurate records of checks performed, in line with clinical governance and audit requirements
* Contribute to a culture of learning by reporting errors and near misses through the appropriate incident-reporting channels
* Support continuous improvement of dispensing accuracy processes, flagging recurring issues or risks
* Work closely with pharmacists, dispensers, and wider operations staff to maintain smooth, safe workflow through the dispensary
* Maintain up-to-date knowledge of relevant SOPs, product recalls, and safety alerts
* Ensure the working environment meets required standards of hygiene, organisation

* Active registration with the General Pharmaceutical Council (GPhC).
* Previous experience working in a pharmacy environment (community, online, or dispensing pharmacy settings).
* Strong attention to detail with a proven ability to maintain high levels of accuracy in a regulated environment.
* Ability to work effectively in a high-volume, fast-paced setting while managing competing priorities and deadlines.
* Confident using IT systems and capable of quickly learning new technologies and software tools.
* Commitment to contributing to a positive, collaborative, and inclusive workplace culture.

## About Hesta
Hesta is setting a new benchmark in women's health, delivering exceptional, evidence-based clinical care at every life stage, starting with pregnancy and the two years after birth. We combine compassionate care with technology built at the forefront of AI-native healthcare.
75 million years of women's lives are lost every year to poor health or early death. Not because these conditions are rare, but because almost no one has been paid to look into them properly. We're changing that.
We raised our pre-seed round last year, alongside grant funding to launch Hesta Labs. Within months of founding we operationalised a CQC-registered multidisciplinary healthcare service, have already cared for hundreds of women, and been featured in The Times.
Cofounders:
* Dr Sujitha Selvarajah: NHS OBGYN doctor with a global public health background. Has worked with the WHO and The Lancet, and is an ex-researcher at Oxford and UCL.
* Amanda Cupples: ex-Managing Director, Airbnb UK, Northern Europe and MEA; ex-COO, Babylon; ex-McKinsey and Deluxe.
Supported by world-leading clinical, product and technology advisors, and backed by investors including Eka, Blue Lion, Ascension and others.
**What women who've used Hesta are saying:**
"Surpassed any expectations. Highly recommend."
"I have never felt this listened to or heard by a GP before. I felt very empowered and supported."
**What clinicians, including GPs, are saying:**
"This is so good. Women won't even need to see the GP with this. This is even better than most GPs."
We're early-stage: genuine ownership, genuine impact, and the chance to build something that doesn't exist yet, that changes millions of lives.
## About Hesta Labs
Hesta Labs is Hesta's research and development arm, backed by £1.4m in grant funding.
In health, there are only two categories of things: what we know, and what we don't. The second category in women’s health is a chasm. Women weren't required to be included in clinical trials until the early 1990s, and even now, only a sliver of health research funding goes towards conditions that affect women specifically..
Hesta's core service proves that operationalising the known changes lives today. But we've come to believe something else just as firmly: you cannot operationalise your way out of a gap this size. If the evidence was never built, the data never captured, the solutions never tested, somebody has to go and build it. That's what Labs is for.
We tested that belief before we committed to it. Using an Innovate UK grant, we ran a feasibility study with Modality Partnership, delivering care to hundreds of women across East Surrey, Yorkshire and Birmingham, and asked three questions: is this clinically valuable, is this technically possible, and do women actually love it? We found yes, yes and yes.
Labs runs on three principles: invest in the unknown, play and experiment with rigour, and seek out the data that actually changes care. Today that means our current feasibility study under the 2025 Femtech & AI programme, and our newly awarded Innovate UK Biomedical Catalyst grant, over £1.4m, taking Hesta from a validated feasibility study to a scalable repeatable solution.
## The role
We're hiring a Founding Associate for Hesta Labs.
You have to be hungry. Hungry for this role, hungry to make a difference, hungry to get things done and bring people with you.
We want a generalist who can move fluidly between clinical, technical, regulatory and commercial workstreams, who turns ambiguity into a plan without waiting to be told how.
You'll work directly with founders, clinicians and technical team members, and across a high-calibre network of partners: NHS Trusts, academic institutions, regulatory advisors and specialist clinicians. Your job is to turn the oxymoron of ambitiguity and clear vision into a delivered, regulator-ready product and evidence base, in the most time- and cost-efficient way possible.
## What you'll do
* Lead our Innovate UK Biomedical Catalyst programme (£1.4m, 18 months) end to end, owning milestones, dependencies and outputs.
* Solve whatever's in the way: designing a communication sequence, onboarding a trial site, sorting a data flow, working out what a regulatory requirement means for us in practice.
* Coordinate across multiple workstreams (clinical, technical, regulatory, commercial), managing interdependencies and critical paths.
* Stay on top of the numbers: own financial planning and data-driven project metrics.
* Steer the path from product and research findings to a regulated, Software as a Medical Device (SaMD).
* Define the plan alongside our Co-Founders, flag risks early, and handle reporting and financial management, including formal change requests where scope or budget shifts.
* Drive alignment and action across internal teams, NHS partners, academic collaborators and external suppliers.
* Feed what we're learning back into product and go-to-market decisions.
* Contribute to future strategy and shaping Hesta's R&D roadmap.
## What you'll bring
* A high-agency, "make it happen" mindset. You must be able to demonstrate the ability to use initiative.
* Strong programme or project experience in complex, multi-stakeholder environments (health tech, research, consulting or innovation). You're equally comfortable with clinicians, academics, engineers and commercial teams, all in the same week.
* Excellent quantitative skills. You’re not put off by a spreadsheet and can build metrics to track progress.
* A proven ability to manage complex dependencies and deliver outcomes, not just track tasks.
* Exceptional organisation and documentation skills. You create clarity and structure in ambiguity.
* The ability to operate in regulated, high-rigour environments, or a strong appetite to learn fast.
Bonus:
* Experience with digital health, SaMD or clinical research.
* Familiarity with NHS systems, data governance or regulatory frameworks.
* Exposure to health economics or evaluation studies.
## Before you apply
Tell us about a time you got something done that mattered, where nobody gave you permission to start it, and nobody had to push you to finish it. What was it, why did you do it, and what happened?
## The practicalities
* Contract: full time.
* Location: London, hybrid. 2 to 3 days a week in person at our office in Victoria, SW1.
* Start: November 2026
## What you'll get
* A front-row seat in an early-stage, mission-driven company building the backbone of a healthcare service designed specifically for women.
* The chance to lead delivery of a major Innovate UK-funded R&D programme shaping the future of women's health.
* A central role in building a regulated, category-defining health technology from the ground up.
* Exposure to clinical, technical, regulatory and commercial strategy in a fast-moving startup.
* A high-calibre, mission-driven team with deep expertise across healthcare and technology.
* Flexible, hybrid working, built around the job that needs doing, not office face time.
* Office facilities: spacious working space alongside other innovators in Victoria, bike storage, changing facilities, and a healthy supply of tea and coffee.
We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and those from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

# Air Source Heat Pump Service Engineer
## Service, diagnose and optimise domestic air source heat pump systems across Devon and Cornwall, keeping homes warm and systems running smoothly.
**£35,000–£45,000 Salary Equivalent + Performance Incentives | Company Van | Private Medical Insurance | Paid Travel Time**
**Location:** Ideally located within reasonable travelling distance of Exeter or Helston **Pay:** £35,000–£45,000 salary equivalent, depending on experience, based on a 40-hour working week. Performance incentives and overtime provide the opportunity to achieve higher on-target earnings. **Job Type:** Full-time
## **Join One of the South West’s Leading Renewable Heating Teams**
GreenGenUK is continuing to expand across Devon and Cornwall, and we are looking for an experienced Air Source Heat Pump Service Engineer to join our growing service and maintenance team.
Established in 2011, GreenGenUK has become one of the South West’s leading renewable-energy installers and is proud to be part of the Hometree Group. With more than 50 directly employed team members, a substantial installed customer base and continued investment in our people, there has never been a better time to join us.
We install and maintain hundreds of renewable-heating systems each year and now support more than 1,000 heat pump customers. Our reputation has been built on quality workmanship, strong technical knowledge and excellent customer service.
This is a new, full-time position created as our service and maintenance workload continues to grow.
## **Why Join GreenGenUK?**
✔ South West Renewable Heating Installer of the Year 2025 ✔ Established renewable-energy business with over 50 employees **✔** Part of the Hometree Group ✔ Large and growing heat pump customer base ✔ Strong pipeline of planned service and maintenance work ✔ Company van and paid travel time ✔ Private medical insurance ✔ Performance incentives and overtime opportunities ✔ Working-away opportunities with enhanced rates ✔ Manufacturer training and support for individual systems ✔ Support from an experienced in-house technical team ✔ Long-term job security within a growing sector
## **The Role**
You will carry out planned servicing, fault diagnosis, repairs and performance optimisation on domestic air source heat pump systems throughout Devon and Cornwall.
This is primarily a service and maintenance role. You will need to understand and assess the complete heating system rather than considering the heat pump in isolation. This includes the heat pump, heating controls, hot-water cylinder, pumps, valves, emitters, electrical components and system hydraulics.
**Your work will include:**
* Planned annual servicing of air source heat pump systems
* Attending breakdowns and investigating reported faults
* Mechanical, hydraulic, electrical and controls-based fault finding
* Repairing or replacing defective system components
* Diagnosing poor performance, high energy consumption or comfort issues
* Checking and optimising weather compensation and heating curves
* Reviewing flow temperatures, system pressures, flow rates and temperature differentials
* Inspecting cylinders, pumps, valves, filters, expansion vessels and heating controls
* Completing commissioning checks following installations or remedial works
* Carrying out warranty inspections and manufacturer-authorised remedial work
* Identifying additional repairs and providing clear information for quotations
* Liaising with manufacturers, technical support and our internal operations team
* Explaining system operation clearly to customers
* Providing customers with practical advice on using their system efficiently
* Completing electronic job sheets, photographs, test results and service records
* Maintaining suitable van stock, tools and test equipment
* Supporting installation teams with technical fault finding when required
You will work on systems from manufacturers including Mitsubishi Electric, Vaillant, Samsung and other established heat pump brands.
You do not need previous experience with every system we work on. GreenGenUK will provide manufacturer training and ongoing technical support for individual products and systems.
The role includes paid travel throughout The South West.
## **What We’re Looking For**
We are looking for an experienced and methodical heating engineer who enjoys fault finding and takes pride in resolving problems properly.
You should be confident working independently in customers’ homes while knowing when to seek assistance from manufacturers or GreenGenUK’s wider technical team.
**The successful candidate should have:**
* Practical experience servicing, commissioning or repairing air source heat pumps
* NVQ Level 2 plumbing and heating qualification as a minimum, with Level 3 preferred
* G3 Unvented Hot Water qualification
* Strong knowledge of domestic wet central-heating and hot-water systems
* Good electrical and controls-based fault-finding ability
* An understanding of system balancing, flow rates and weather compensation
* The ability to interpret technical manuals, wiring diagrams and system schematics
* A logical and methodical approach to diagnosing faults
* Strong customer-facing and communication skills
* The ability to explain technical issues in straightforward language
* Confidence using a mobile phone or tablet to complete service records
* The ability to work independently and manage a field-based workload
* A professional attitude and commitment to high-quality workmanship
* A full UK driving licence
## **Desirable Experience**
**The following would be advantageous, although manufacturer and product-specific training will be provided:**
* Mitsubishi Ecodan experience or manufacturer training
* Vaillant aroTHERM experience or manufacturer training
* Samsung heat pump experience or manufacturer training
* Experience working with R290 heat pump systems
* A recognised heat pump installation or service qualification
* Electrical qualifications or formal electrical fault-finding training
* Water Regulations qualification
* F-Gas and/or hydrocarbon refrigerant training
* Experience with underfloor heating and multi-zone heating controls
* Familiarity with MCS standards and renewable-heating commissioning documents
## **What We Offer**
* £35,000–£45,000 salary equivalent, depending on experience
* Performance-related incentives offering the opportunity to earn more
* 40-hour working week
* Paid travel time
* Overtime opportunities
* Enhanced rates for working away
* Company van
* Company pension scheme
* Private medical insurance
* 28 days’ holiday including bank holidays
* Company workwear and PPE
* Tools and test equipment
* Manufacturer training and ongoing support for individual systems
* Support from an experienced operations and technical team
## **Equal Opportunity Employer**
At GreenGenUK, we are committed to creating an inclusive and representative working environment. We know that different experiences, perspectives and backgrounds create a better workplace and a stronger business.
We provide equal opportunities throughout our recruitment process and working environment. Employment decisions are based on experience, skills and suitability for the role.
## **Ready for a New Challenge?**
If you are an experienced engineer who enjoys fault finding, takes pride in delivering excellent customer service and wants to develop within the renewable-heating sector, we would love to hear from you.

# Systems and Customer Journey Manager
## Own the systems and customer journeys behind our installer businesses, improving CRM, processes and technology to deliver better customer experiences.
**Salary:** Up to £65,000 depending on experience **Role type:** Permanent, 5 days per week, Monday to Friday **Location:** Hybrid, based at our London office, with occasional travel to our installer businesses **Reporting to:** Sales Operations Director (Installs) or Operations Director (Installs) **Direct Reports:** None
## **About Hometree**
Join Hometree at the most exciting moment in our story. Founded in 2015, we've become one of the fastest-growing challengers in the UK home services market, spanning home cover that protects the essential systems in the home, renewable installations like solar, batteries and heat pumps, and the financing that makes them affordable. Together, we help homeowners look after their homes and move to greener, lower-carbon living.
We're now going through the biggest step change in our history. By acquiring OVO Energy's Home Services division, including the trusted CORGI HomePlan and HomeHeat brands, we're becoming one of the UK's leading home services groups, with fresh investment to fuel our next phase of growth. It's a genuine inflection point, and we're looking for people who want to help us build what comes next.
### **Key Achievements**
🏆 UK's third-largest home cover provider: our latest acquisition makes us the third-largest provider of home cover in the UK.
🏆 7 Acquisitions - We've expanded our operations by acquiring 6 key companies across financing (Hometree Finance, formerly Bewarm), Home Cover (Your Repair) and energy services (Geowarmth, The Little Green Energy Company, IMS and GreenGen). And we have most recently announced the acquisition of OVO Home Services and CORGI Homeplan (subject to FCA approval).
🏆 500k Homes Covered - We cover over 500 thousand homes across the UK.
🏆 550+ Employees - We have over 550 passionate employees transforming the industry across the Group, one home at a time.
## **The Role**
You'll own how our systems and processes work for the customer, across our renewables and gas boiler installer businesses: heat pumps, solar, batteries and boiler installs.
You decide what good looks like: how the customer journey should flow, how our CRM and customer communications should work, and where the systems portfolio needs to change so each business can grow. That means getting into the detail of how things work today, finding where we're letting customers down, and building the fix.
Sometimes the fix is new software, not a tweak to what we've got. Where there's a real gap, you'll lead the search: work out what we need, scan the market, and build the case to buy. Once we've chosen, you'll see it through to delivery too, working with Technology, the vendor and the teams who'll use it day to day. You won't write the code, but you'll make sure it lands.
AI is part of this as well. You'll find where it could improve the customer journey, test what looks promising, and bring what works into everyday use. You don't need to have done this before. You do need to be up for it.
You'll usually have more than one of these live at once, pulling in different directions across different businesses. Being methodical matters: work to a plan, keep it on track, and build a clear framework, with your manager's support, for what gets priority when everything feels urgent.
There's a natural link to Home Cover too, particularly insurance and maintenance cross-sell. That's a collaboration, not a responsibility: you'll work with the Home Cover team to align on those journeys and maximise sales both ways.
You'll report to our Sales Operations Director (Installs) or Operations Director (Installs), with a dotted line to our CTO or Head of Product. It's a broad role with real ownership, and it'll suit someone from consulting, a fast-growing business, or already running CRM and systems somewhere else, who wants to turn our systems and customer journeys into something concrete.
## **Responsibilities**
* **Systems Portfolio:** Own the ongoing design of our systems portfolio across customer-facing and internal systems for our renewables and gas boiler installer businesses, including CRM and customer communications, setting the roadmap even when someone else builds it.
* **Process Mapping:** Map how customers and information actually move through our installer businesses today, identifying where a process, system or message is letting customers or growth down.
* **Customer Journey:** Redesign the customer journey from first enquiry through to installation and aftercare, working closely with Sales, Operations and Marketing so everyone's pulling in the same direction.
* **CRM & Communications:** Own the CRM roadmap and customer communications approach for our installer businesses, understanding what each one genuinely needs.
* **Cross-Sell Journeys:** Work with our Home Cover business to align insurance and maintenance cross-sell journeys with installer customers, while creating installation opportunities from Home Cover journeys.
* **Prioritisation:** Build and maintain a framework for prioritising competing work across the systems and customer journey portfolio, agreeing where to focus when priorities conflict.
* **Data & Testing:** Dig into the data to understand what's happening, form hypotheses about what would improve things, and test them before recommending a wider rollout.
* **System Selection:** Lead the search for new systems or software where there's a genuine gap, from scoping requirements and evaluating the market to making the investment case.
* **Implementation:** Help see chosen solutions through to delivery, working with Technology, vendors and the teams using them day to day to get them properly live.
* **AI & Innovation:** Explore, test and help deploy AI within our customer journeys and systems, identifying where it can genuinely improve things for the customer or business.
* **Product & Technology:** Work with the CTO or Head of Product and their teams to turn business needs into solutions they can build, staying involved to ensure the end result works for the customer.
* **Stakeholder Management:** Build strong working relationships across Commercial, Operations, Sales, Marketing, Finance and Technology, at Group level and within each installer business.
* **Commercial Impact:** Spot changes, big or small, that could grow sales or protect revenue, and back recommendations up with evidence.
## **What we're looking for**
* **Problem Solving:** Experience taking on broad, loosely defined problems and turning them into a clear, practical plan, whatever industry or role that came from.
* **Methodical Approach:** Comfortable working to a plan, keeping it on track, and building a clear framework for prioritising work when multiple pieces compete for your attention.
* **Process Mapping:** A track record of mapping out business or customer processes and turning that into a real recommendation, not just a diagram.
* **Data & Analysis:** Comfortable pulling data apart, forming a view, and checking whether that view holds up once you test it.
* **CRM & Customer Communications:** Some exposure to CRM platforms and customer communications, including deciding how they should work and understanding how to configure or structure solutions.
* **Systems & Software:** Experience choosing between software or system options, making the case for one, and staying involved through build and rollout.
* **Stakeholder Management:** Able to hold your own with directors and executives while still getting stuck in with teams doing the day-to-day work.
* **Autonomy:** Happy working independently across more than one business without being handed a ready-made playbook.
* **AI Mindset:** Genuinely open to exploring and adopting AI in how we work, even without direct experience.
* **Clear Communication:** Able to explain systems or data points clearly to someone who has never looked at the detail before.
## **Extra Credit**
* Background in strategy consulting or another broad, generalist commercial role
* Experience working across multiple business units or brands, ideally inside a group that's grown through acquisition
* Hands-on experience with CRM platforms such as Monday.com & Simpro
* Experience in home services, energy, renewables or another regulated consumer sector
* Experience designing customer journeys or communications within a business regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority
* Experience running a software selection process from scratch, from the initial business case through to choosing a vendor and getting it live
* Experience exploring, testing or deploying AI tools within customer journeys, CRM or business systems
* Training or a qualification in process mapping, change management or product management
## **Our Recruitment Process**
* Initial Call: Start with an introductory call with our Talent Acquisition team to discuss the role and your potential fit (30 mins)
* Skills-Based Interview: A detailed discussion about your experience mapping processes, working with data and managing stakeholders, with the hiring manager (1 hour)
* Task Stage: Present a task to our Commercial and Technology stakeholders (1 hour)
* Values Interview: A Values Based Interview with 2 employees, typically stakeholders you'll work with (40 mins)
* Final Interview: For certain positions there may be a final interview with a member of senior management or our senior leadership team (30 mins)
## **Perks of the job**
We have an ever expanding list of benefits that currently includes:
* 25 days holiday plus bank holidays and your birthday
* Hybrid working, based at our London office
* Free boiler & home emergency cover with Hometree plus 40% discount for friends & family
* Discounted gym membership across over 100 UK gyms (independent and chains) and free fitness, wellness and nutrition apps

At Hometree, we prioritise ethical conduct and regulatory compliance. As a regulated financial services organisation, we operate under the strict guidelines and regulations set forth by the Financial Conduct Authority. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of integrity and professionalism in all aspects of our business.
As a prospective member of our team, you will be expected to fully embrace and adhere to the Financial Conduct Authority Code of Conduct obligations. These obligations are designed to ensure the fair treatment of customers, the preservation of market integrity, and the promotion of healthy competition within the financial services industry.

* Comfort checking performance data and knowing what to do with it.
* Interest in brand positioning and localisation, going beyond translation to what actually resonates.

💸 Paid Employee Referral Scheme

You’ll work closely with customers and teams across Sales, Customer Success, Product and Engineering. Improve our implementation approach by introducing AI-enabled workflows, refining playbooks and sharing recurring patterns, friction points and product feedback with Product and Engineering.

A strong record of delivering projects on time and within scope while managing multiple workstreams and stakeholders.
Exceptional attention to detail, particularly when handling data migration, validation and product configuration.
Practical experience using AI to materially improve implementation work, with clear examples of what changed and the impact it delivered.
Confidence working with integrations, APIs and webhooks, with the ability to explain technical requirements clearly to customers.
Strong working knowledge of Google Sheets or Excel and the ability to learn new systems and tools quickly.

Comfort operating in an environment where processes are still developing and you are expected to improve them through hands-on experience.

# Consultant, Value, Pricing & Market Access (Life Sciences) - UK
London, United Kingdom
**The Opportunity**
Join Putnam’s Value, Pricing & Market Access (VPA) practice and help leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies navigate some of their most important commercialization and access challenges.
As a Consultant, you will play a key role on client engagements focused on pricing, market access, value strategy, launch planning, payer strategy, and commercialization. You will work closely with clients and Putnam leadership while guiding project teams, structuring complex problems, developing insights, and translating analysis into actionable recommendations.
This is an opportunity for someone with life sciences and/or consulting experience who is ready to take on greater responsibility, deepen their expertise in value and market access, and have meaningful exposure to senior clients and firm leaders.
**What You’ll Do**
As a Consultant within our Value, Pricing & Market Access practice, you will:
* Partner with clients to understand complex business challenges and develop hypotheses and strategic approaches to address them.
* Structure and solve strategic and analytical problems related to pricing, market access, payer strategy, value proposition, launch strategy, and commercialization.
* Lead the day-to-day execution of client engagements, coordinating workstreams and helping project teams stay focused on key objectives.
* Guide and mentor Associates and Life Sciences Consultants, providing direction, feedback, and support throughout engagements.
* Conduct and synthesize quantitative and qualitative analyses to identify meaningful insights and implications.
* Translate complex findings into clear, compelling, and actionable recommendations for clients.
* Develop high-quality client presentations and participate in client meetings, workshops, and presentations.
* Collaborate closely with Putnam Partners, Principals, and colleagues across our broader global health and life sciences organization.
* Build expertise across therapeutic areas, market access challenges, and evolving trends shaping the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries.
**What We’re Looking For**
We recognize that great candidates bring different combinations of experience and expertise. You may be a strong fit if you have:
* Relevant professional experience in life sciences consulting, pharmaceutical or biotechnology strategy, market access, pricing, commercialization, or a related field.
* A strong understanding of the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry and the factors influencing product value, pricing, reimbursement, and market access.
* Experience analyzing complex business questions and turning data and research into strategic recommendations.
* Strong quantitative, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience developing and presenting clear, compelling recommendations.
* Experience managing projects, workstreams, and/or junior team members.
* The ability to collaborate effectively in a team-oriented, client-service environment.
* Intellectual curiosity and interest in solving complex challenges at the intersection of science, strategy, access, and commercialization.
* An advanced degree such as an MBA, MPH, MS, PharmD, PhD, or other relevant postgraduate degree is welcome but not required.
**About Inizio Ignite, Putnam**
Inizio Ignite is the global advisory partner for health and life sciences, encompassing connected expertise across Research Partnership, Putnam, Vynamic, and STEM. Guided by purpose, passion, and precision, we collaborate with clients to ignite impact, accelerate performance, and deliver lasting change for patients.
Our Putnam strategy consulting team bridges science and strategy to enable confident decision-making and build value for pharma. We partner with leading health and life science companies serving brand & commercial leaders, Medical Affairs, access & pricing, and R&D. Our expertise spans offerings including therapeutic area strategy, data & AI strategy, go-to-market strategy, commercialization & growth, value, pricing & access (VPA) strategy, and evidence generation.
Proudly part of Inizio – the market-leading commercialization partner for health and life sciences. From early-stage development to loss of exclusivity, we simplify complexity, unlock value, and make collaboration seamless at every pivotal moment – supporting confident, insight-driven decisions that move innovation forward.
**Why Putnam**
At Putnam, you’ll have the opportunity to work on high-impact strategic questions for leading health and life sciences companies while developing deep expertise in an industry that directly affects patients around the world.
Our work combines sophisticated quantitative analysis with qualitative research and strategic thinking. Engagements can span value, pricing and access strategy, product and portfolio strategy, market assessment, launch strategy, commercialization and growth, evidence generation, therapeutic area strategy, and R&D strategy.
We offer the entrepreneurial and collaborative environment of a specialized consulting firm with the reach, capabilities, and career opportunities of a global health and life sciences organization.

* Meaningful client exposure and responsibility.
* Opportunities to work alongside experienced life sciences leaders.
* Structured professional development and leadership training.
* Mentorship and opportunities to mentor others.
* Exposure to diverse therapeutic areas and strategic challenges.
* Clear opportunities for career growth and advancement.
* A collaborative, team-oriented culture.
* Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits.

We welcome candidates with different experiences and career paths who share our passion for improving healthcare and solving complex problems.

# Business Analyst (Talent Pool)
at innocent drinks
* London, United Kingdom
* Full Time
* Posted yesterday
Here at innocent, we’re on a mission to make it easier for everyone to get more fruit and veg into their bodies. We started back in 1999 and since then we’ve gone from selling a few smoothies at a music festival to becoming one of Europe’s biggest drinks companies with around 1,000 people (and the B Corp seal of approval).
It’s nice to be able to say things like that but we’re not patting ourselves on the back just yet. We want to show everyone that it’s possible to be a successful business while looking after people and the planet too, so we’re trying to get better in pretty much every way. And that’s where this job comes in.
**A little background**
At innocent, data helps us make better decisions about our drinks, our operations, and how we grow the business responsibly. Our Business Analysts play a big role in this, partnering with teams across the business to turn questions into insights and insights into action.
This advert isn’t for a specific open role right now. Instead, it’s our way of meeting curious, analytical people who’d like to be part of innocent in the future. We’re building a **talent pool** for Business Analyst roles across different levels. From those starting out in their analytics journey to more seasoned analysts looking for their next challenge. This is open to all levels and when a role comes up we’ll match applications.
If you like solving meaningful problems, asking good questions, and working with humans as much as numbers, we’d love to hear from you.
**You’ll be**
Want to hear how this looks in practice? Business Analysts at innocent often:
* Partner with teams across the business to understand challenges and turn them into clear problems and requirements
* Analyse data, processes and systems to uncover insights, opportunities and risks
* Shape solutions by thinking across people, process, technology and data
* Create clear documentation, process maps, and analysis that help drive decisions
* Support or lead delivery across the full project lifecycle, from early concept through to rollout
* Work closely with project teams, engineers, subject matter experts and third‐party partners
* Contribute to testing activities, making sure changes work as expected and issues are resolved
* Help land change effectively through training, communication and ongoing support
* Track progress, manage risks and dependencies, and help keep work on track
* Work with various tools like Azure and Lucid Chart, and work with systems like Dynamics 365 and Kinaxis Maestro.
Depending on your level, you might also:
* Lead end‐to‐end analysis on complex projects
* Influence senior stakeholders and shape decision‐making
* Improve ways of working, governance and delivery standards
* Coach or support more junior analysts
**You’ll have**
Here’s what we’re looking for in our Business Analysts:
* A strong analytical mindset and curiosity for understanding how things work
* Experience working with data, processes or systems (this can look different depending on your level)
* The ability to turn complex information into clear, thoughtful recommendations
* Confidence working with stakeholders and adapting your style to different audiences
* A practical, problem‐solving approach and a desire to make things better
* Attention to detail, with the ability to see things through from idea to delivery
* Comfort using tools (e.g. Excel, reporting tools, systems) and a willingness to keep learning
For more experienced roles, we’ll also look for:
* Experience delivering change end‐to‐end across projects or programmes
* Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills
* The ability to manage multiple priorities and work through ambiguity
* Experience supporting or developing others
You'll get
* The chance to be considered first for future Business Analyst roles at innocent
* Work with a variety of teams on many different projects. Keeping you learning non-stop.
* A role where insights genuinely influence decisions, not just slides
* Support to grow your skills, whether you’re deepening your technical toolkit or your commercial thinking
* The opportunity to do work that supports a business trying to leave things a little better than it found them
We want innocent to be a great place to work, so we do lots of stuff to make people feel at home and try to make sure everyone’s career is shaping up the way they want it to. There are plenty of opportunities to have a go at something new or take things further.
In exchange for helping us do business in the right way, you’ll get a solid rewards package that includes a salary (phew), private healthcare, a target-based bonus, and a bunch of other nice things like a day off on your birthday. And yes, you get free smoothies.
We also know that not all our drinkers come from the same background, or think the same – so why should we? At innocent, we want to be a great place to work where a diverse bunch of people from all backgrounds can turn up and thrive. When we hire, we want all the juice, bits, and pulp that make you who you are.

# Staff Software Engineer (Inference Platform), London
London
Isomorphic Labs is applying frontier AI to help unlock deeper scientific insights, faster breakthroughs, and life-changing medicines with an ambition to solve all disease.
The future is coming. A future enabled and enriched by the incredible power of machine learning. A future in which diseases are curtailed or cured starting with better and faster drug discovery.
Come and be part of an interdisciplinary team driving groundbreaking innovation and play a meaningful role in contributing towards us achieving our ambitious goals, while being a part of an inspiring and collaborative culture.
The world we want tomorrow is the one we’re building today. It starts with the culture at this company. It starts with you.
### **About Iso**
Isomorphic Labs (IsoLabs) was launched in 2021 to advance human health by building on and beyond the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system. Since then, our interdisciplinary team of drug discovery experts and machine learning specialists has built powerful new predictive and generative AI models that accelerate scientific discovery at digital speed.
Our name comes from the belief that there is an underlying symmetry between biology and information science. By harnessing AI’s powerful capabilities, we can use it to model complex biological phenomena to help design novel molecules, anticipate how drugs will perform and develop innovative medicines to treat and cure some of the world’s most devastating diseases.
We have built a world-leading drug design engine comprising AI models that are capable of working across multiple therapeutic areas and drug modalities. We are continually innovating on model architecture and developing cutting-edge capabilities to advance rational drug design.
Every day, and with each new breakthrough, we’re getting closer to the promise of digital biology, and achieving our ambitious mission to one day solve all disease with the help of AI.
**Your Impact**
We are building the largest foundation models in biotech and applying them immediately to cure disease. You will play a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and scalability of the foundations that make this possible.
As a Principal Engineer, you will lead the efforts to harden our systems, ensuring our groundbreaking AI is built on an unshakeable base, working closely with the research team and the Applied ML teams to ensure the infrastructure is stable, reliable and can operate with more data and larger models as we grow.
**What You Will Do**
* Develop and operate our inference platform, serving fleets of cutting-edge machine learning models to scientific applications.
* Design strategy and build roadmaps for maturing the platform.
* Architect and optimize our next-generation inference services. You will solve core scaling limits, ensuring high-throughput performance and feature parity across our model serving stack.
* Contribute to core technical decisions on tooling and architectural design while partnering with science, product, and operations teams to align infrastructure with biotech R&D cycles.
* Deliver high-quality and well-tested user-focused features.
**Skills and Qualifications**
**Essential:**
* Proven experience in architecting and managing large-scale AI/ML workloads in a production environment.
* Orchestration: Significant experience deploying and managing complex workloads within Kubernetes (GKE).
* Expertise in cloud compute design, specifically within Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
* Professional familiarity with NVIDIA GPU generations and the intricacies of high-performance compute.
* Strong programming skills and a "reliability-first" approach to software development.
**Nice to Have:**
* A career history that spans both ML Software Engineering and Infrastructure SRE roles.
* Experience leading multi-disciplinary projects and navigating complex stakeholder requirements in a fast-paced environment.
* Familiarity with workload scheduling, ML efficiency research, and hardware benchmarking.
* Experience with Google TPU generations and specialized ML-driven R&D cycles.
### **Culture and values**
We are guided by our shared values. It's not about finding people who think and act in the same way. These values help to guide our work and will continue to strengthen it.
**Thoughtful**Thoughtful at Iso is about curiosity, creativity and care. It is about good people doing good, rigorous and future-making science every single day.
**Brave**Brave at Iso is about fearlessness, but it’s also about initiative and integrity. The scale of the challenge demands nothing less.
**Determined**Determined at Iso is the way we pursue our goal. It’s a confidence in our hypothesis, as well as the urgency and agility needed to deliver on it. Because disease won’t wait, so neither should we.
**Together**Together at Iso is about connection, collaboration across fields and catalytic relationships. It’s knowing that transformation is a group project, and remembering that what we’re doing will have a real impact on real people everywhere.
### **Creating an extraordinary company**
We believe that to be successful we need a team with a range of skills and talents. We're building an environment where collaboration is fundamental, learning is shared and every employee feels supported and able to thrive. We value unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, and perspectives, and harness these qualities to create extraordinary impact.
We are committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis protected by applicable law. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.
### **Hybrid working**
It’s hugely important for us to share knowledge and build strong relationships with each other, and we find it easier to do this if we spend time together in person. This is why we follow a hybrid model, and **would require you to be able to come into the office 3 days a week** (currently Tuesday, Wednesday, and one other day depending on which team you’re in). If you have additional needs that would prevent you from following this hybrid approach, we’d be happy to talk through these if you’re selected for an initial screening call.

**Senior Counsel, Legal – AI Governance, Data Privacy, & Cybersecurity**
As the Senior Counsel, Legal – AI Governance, Data Privacy, & Cybersecurity, you will serve as the legal lead and manage the legal side of these programs for a global company operating in multiple jurisdictions. In this role, you will report to the Vice President, Legal – Litigation & Compliance
**AI Governance** – you will maintain a global AI Governance program and advise on AI-specific laws (such as the EU AI Act) as well as AI Governance generally, providing legal and business advice that is risk-conscious while encouraging responsible AI development and use. You will coordinate a cross-functional team that includes attorneys and cyber risk professionals and maintain an internal website resource that provides guidance and updates.
**Data Privacy** – you will maintain a global Data Privacy program and advise on data privacy laws (including the GDPR, UK Data Protection Act 2018/UK GDPR, and laws in other jurisdictions such as the US, Saudi Arabia, China, and California). You will provide advice on contracts with vendors and customers, and you will lead the response to data subject requests, coordinating with Human Resources professionals, management, and other attorneys.
**Cybersecurity** – you will coordinate with the Chief Information Security Office’s team to address legal cybersecurity risk. You will also assist with analysis of data events to determine whether any personal data breach or non-personal data breach reporting requirements, either statutory or contractual, are implicated, working together with other attorneys and stakeholders.
**Insider Threat** – you will assist in assessing and coordinating responses to potential insider threats and managing the company’s global insider threat program, working with other attorneys, management, and insider threat support professionals from the IT team.
**Required Qualifications:**
* Law degree and admission to practice in the UK or an EU member state
* A relevant number of years PQE
* Comprehensive expertise in the AI, data privacy and cybersecurity laws of many jurisdictions
* Strong grasp of ISO 27701 or similar data privacy frameworks and working knowledge of adjacent frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001)
* Strong change management skills, including the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and countries and to design and implement efficient, sustainable processes and tools
* Ability to communicate key issues in simple, succinct ways and to pivot and respond to stakeholders’ questions and challenges

* Track record of increasing your effectiveness and productivity through using approved AI systems for work
* Managing outside counsel to deliver value

* Familiarity with AI-specific laws, AI-related laws, Data Privacy laws, and Cybersecurity laws
* Experience advising clients on business and legal risk in a risk-conscious but business-focused approach
* Motivation and initiative in researching and distilling new laws and laws from various jurisdictions into sound legal and business advice
* Sound judgment and confidence addressing sensitive insider threat situations
* Patience and understanding of cultural differences in a global business environment
**Preferred Qualifications:**
* CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPP/A, and CIPM certifications from the International Association of Privacy Professionals
* AI Governance Professional (AIGP) certification from the International Association of Privacy Professionals
* Experience with internal investigations, employment law, IP law or litigation
**KBR Company Information**

## Description
Landytech is on a mission to revolutionise the way that investment managers, asset owners and their advisors access asset information. Powered by Sesame, an industry-leading investment reporting platform, we are helping clients in over 15 countries make informed investment decisions and deliver insights faster.
The company is growing rapidly and it’s an exciting time to join, having secured $12M in Series B funding in January 2023. In just four years, it has gone from two co-founders to a team of 80+ staff, with offices in London and Paris. At Landytech, we see diversity as our strength with a team from over 15 countries and 14 languages spoken.
**The role**
AI has made producing screens easy. It has not made products coherent. We are looking for someone to own the experience of Sesame end to end — the client journey, the interaction logic, the look and feel, and the consistency of all of it — and to build it.
If you are an engineer who has always had a view on how the product should look and behave, this is a role where that judgement is part of the remit rather than a side interest.
*We have posted this role under two titles — Design Engineer and Product Experience Designer — to reach both backgrounds. Same role, same team. Apply once, to whichever fits you better.*
**How we work**
We have rebuilt our product process around AI rather than bolting it on:
• AI is used heavily at every stage of both design and engineering, not just at the production end
• Our design system lives in code, used by engineers and AI tooling alike
• Tooling changes every few months and we expect it to
You will have real scope to shape how we work, and to help build the parts that do not exist yet.
**What you will shape**
How much of this you lead outright will depend on your experience and on how it fits with the team already in place. There is room to take on more over time.
* **The front-end experience layer.** You will build the interfaces that matter most, particularly the dense and difficult ones, and help set the patterns others follow
* **The design system.** Developed in code with the rest of the front-end team, with a leading voice in what belongs in the system
* **Look, feel and consistency.** The product should feel like one thing, and you will help define what that one thing is and uphold it in review and in tooling
* **The client journey.** You will be in front of investment professionals, family offices and their advisors, and trusted to act on what you hear
* **Craft in dense financial interfaces.** Tables legible at scale, numbers at the right precision, drill-downs that survive a messy real portfolio under load
**The must-have: setting the standard AI works to**
AI is very good at producing attractive interfaces. Given a design system, almost anyone can now generate a credible screen.
The harder problem, and the one this role exists to solve, is making sure what we build expresses the product’s logic, density and intent rather than simply reusing its components. That means defining the standards and instructions our tools work to, reading the output critically enough to see why something is subtly wrong, and tightening the rules so it does not recur.
Using AI to produce interfaces is not the skill we are looking for. Directing it to our standard, consistently and at depth, is.
Increasingly this is engineering work: it lives in the repo, in the tooling, and in what the agents can and cannot reach for.
**Strongly valued: design expertise**
We are not looking for a front-end engineer willing to tolerate design work. We are looking for real UX judgement.
* You can say what is wrong with a flow, not just implement it faster
* You think in objects, relationships and states before components
* You have taste in what matters here: hierarchy, typography, density, restraint
* You are comfortable doing the upstream thinking, including what should not exist at all
No portfolio required. Shipped interfaces we can look at, and the decisions behind them, is what we want to see.
**Also valued: product management instincts**
If you have talked to clients directly, decided what not to build, and owned an outcome rather than a ticket, we will weight it heavily.
**What we are looking for**
We do not expect anyone to have everything below — we would rather meet someone exceptional in two areas than adequate in all three.
* 5+ years in front-end engineering, ideally React and TypeScript, with libraries such as shadcn/ui
* Experience building and maintaining a design system in production, not just consuming one
* Data-dense interfaces at scale — virtualised tables, charting, performance under real load
* Fluency with AI-assisted development, and the specification skill described above
* Willingness to work directly with users and own the experience, not the implementation alone
* Comfortable as an editor and enabler: reviewing others’ work, teaching, holding a line
* Genuine curiosity about finance. You need not arrive knowing what a capital call is
**Our process**
Our interview process is likely to include a portfolio or work conversation, a short practical exercise based on a real Sesame flow, and a working session with a product manager and an engineer. We adapt the steps to the candidate and will always tell you what to expect in advance.

* Cycle to Work scheme and gym allowance
* Office food and drinks, regular socials

* Collaborate with the inventory management team to implement guidelines for stock control.

You'll make sense of insight, shape prioritisation and design choices, and orchestrate across functional boundaries to ensure journeys are effective end to end. We're looking for a Director of Analytics to lead our lean, multi-disciplined, best-in-class analytics team. You will provide technical direction on product analytics, experimentation, attribution, forecasting, and manage analytical frameworks. You will also evangelise and inspire best practices across the company.
You will report to the Chief Commercial Officer and work closely with the Director of Data Platform and Directors in other functions such as Product, Engineering, Partnerships, Finance and Marketing. Our stack includes AWS, Snowflake, dbt, Looker, Python, R and other best in class, modern tooling for business reporting, experimentation, and analysis. **Leadership and Team Management:**

* Foster a culture of deep analysis, commercial sense, innovation, best practices and evangelizing non-obvious insights (not simply reporting data)
* Align team objectives with company goals and strategic initiatives
* Apply strong commercial intuition, customer-focus and data analysis to drive strategic decision-making

* Provide expert guidance on horizontal technical analytical areas, including experimentation, attribution, forecasting, predictive analytics, and observability

* Identify and track appropriate metrics to measure success across all areas of the business
* Ensure trustworthiness and timeliness of data used by stakeholders from all departments of the company
**Analytics and Strategy:**
* Collaborate with senior leadership to provide insights for decision-making around key initiatives and strategic objectives
* Work with FP&A and product leads to align customer impact with commercial outcomes - working to a common growth-model/metric tree

**Data Strategy and Governance:**
* Partner with the Director of Data Platform to define and execute the vision for how data can be leveraged effectively across the business

* Empower the team to execute on reporting, analytics, and experimentation
* Drive with product development to identify and apply new data opportunities
* Drive understanding of key metrics and their importance across the business

* Expertise in doing analytical work, including data modelling, experimentation, attribution, forecasting, and observability
* Experience leading product analytics and improving product experience based on analysis and insights

* Experience driving change through analytics and data initiatives
* Strong in both high-level strategic thinking and detailed analysis

* Performing joint inspections when required.
* Supporting the monitoring and technical resolution of non-conformances including the management of corrections and corrective actions.
* Supporting the review and acceptance of end of manufacturing reports (EoMR), end of construction status reports (ECSR) and end of erection status reports (EESR).

* Producing quality documentation (e.g. specifications, procedures) as required.

* A team player who recognises how their position impacts and influences others.
* Pro-active and flexible, being prepared to plan and work on own initiative.
* Fluent in English language.
* Knowledge of the nuclear sector, ideally new build.
* Knowledge and understanding of nuclear site license conditions.
* Ability to speak French is advantageous.
* Knowledge of pressure and nuclear codes knowledge of welding, non-destructive testing (NDT), non-destructive evaluation (NDE)

But we’re only just getting started. Our goal is to become one of the largest financial services providers in the world. Over the next 10 years we’ll grow exponentially, not only by scaling our existing products, but also by building new ones.

# **Pricing at Marshmallow**
This role will sit in the Pricing Team, reporting into the Pricing Data Science Manager. The team is responsible for managing our loss ratio, underwriting footprint, broker optimisation and growth targets, proving integral to driving the business forwards. But you’ve probably read that all before! So what’s new?
We work in a very different way to most pricing teams that you might be familiar with. Everyone in Pricing has the potential to make significant contribution to the business, taking ownership, moving fast, innovating and delivering changes to our rates at high frequency.
We don’t just churn out GLMs all day. We build & deploy exceptional in-house pricing data science models using the latest modelling techniques. You’ll work alongside other Pricing Data Scientists & Analysts pushing innovative pricing projects, whilst also being able to work with the wider Data Science community on modelling customer behaviour, fraud & MLENG enhancements.
We work alongside a bunch of amazing engineers who ensure we can implement our decisions quickly. We also have access to huge amounts of data. We don’t just mean your standard policy, claims and quote data. Our engineers spend their lives building APIs to third parties so that we know more about our customers than any of our competitors.
All of this means that you’ll have access to as much data as you can handle, the freedom to be creative, the backing of senior leaders to make decisions, and the ability to see your ideas implemented rapidly. And on top of all of that, we’re a pretty fun group to hang around with!

* Developing a deep understanding of Marshmallow’s quote, policy and claims data and use this to derive insights that can be used to enhance our pricing.
* Own one of the strategic initiatives of the pricing team, such as supporting our expansion plans or protecting our renewing customers.
* Conducting claims analysis and claims modelling using SQL and Python.
* Conducting price optimisation analysis/modelling using Python.
* Building and deploying models in APIs for use in real time pricing.
* Identify new sources of external data that enable us to refine our view of claims risk, and conduct analysis to quantify their value.
* Working directly with our Engineering & MLENG functions to implement pricing proposals.
* Providing pricing support for the launch of multiple new products.

* **Modeller**: You use your DS expertise to build innovative best in class models
* **Commercial**: You directly use your models as tools to deliver timely real world impact
* **Curious**: You aren’t satisfied with ‘That’s just how it is’; you immediately investigate further
* **Owner**: You don’t just pull existing levers - you own end to end transformation in your area
* **Opinionated**: You generate your own opinions & pitch to others in an open & honest way
* **Explainer**: You can communicate complicated concepts in a simple way to non-experts
* **Networker**: You build and maintain strong relationships throughout the business
## **What skills are we looking for from you?**
* Ability to interrogate data and conduct pricing analysis within SQL & Python/R
* Ability to build GLMs, GBMs and other claims models within Python/R
* At least 3 years of experience working in a data driven (ideally commercial) role

* Private medical insurance with Vitality, mental health support with Oliva
* Personal learning budget and 2 dedicated L&D days a year
* Monthly flexible benefits budget to spend as you choose

Dex runs on data. Microsoft Research AI for Science seeks a motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to design and lead experimental data-generation campaigns for the next Biomolecular Emulator (BioEmu) model. The BioEmu project aims to model the dynamics and function of proteins, how they change shape, bind to each other, and bind small molecules. This approach will help us to understand biological function and dysfunction on a structural level and lead to more effective and targeted drug discovery. Our BioEmu-1 model was published in Science (see our blog post for links to our open-source software and other resources and this explainer video). # Operations Associate

Hybrid - London (three core office days each week)Full-time£35,000–£45,000
Reporting to the CEO, working closely with the COO and wider team.
